- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 75+ → 76+).
- Model underreacts to downward trends; fails to adjust forecast mean downward when recent prices show clear decline.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — forecasts stay too high even after 2–3 consecutive days of falling prices.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- Model exhibits lag in correcting for recent low prices — often takes 2–3 days to drop below recent low.
- Overshoots are more common after spikes in history, especially when spike is followed by a sharp drop.
- Model tends to ignore short-term volatility and overweights long-term trends, leading to overconfidence in direction.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model reduces initial overshoot and incorporates recent low prices more aggressively.
